name: Parsley

companions.note: Parsley is said to improve tomato flavor and repel asparagus beetle
Both attract beneficial insects; good herb bed companions

frost_hardiness.notes: Biennial that overwinters reliably in zone 8b. Slows in deep winter but survives and continues producing.

pnw_notes: Biennial — first year it produces leaves, second year it flowers and sets seed before dying. In zone 8b it overwinters reliably and produces heavily in its first spring. Germination is notoriously slow (3–6 weeks); soaking seeds overnight speeds this up. Flat-leaf (Italian) parsley has better flavor than curly; curly is more cold-hardy. Both work here.

planting_windows.notes: Start indoors 8–10 weeks before transplant; soak seeds overnight before sowing
Transplant before first frost; will overwinter and flush with growth in spring
Spring direct sow is slower but works; expect 3–6 weeks to germination
Harvest outer stems continuously; never take more than a third of the plant at once
